title: Coordinate Junta Dependence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a set of coordinates. Form a function by averaging $f$ over independent uniform choices of the coordinates outside $J$, while keeping the coordinates in $J$ fixed, and then taking the sign of that average, with zero assigned the positive sign. Its real-valued form depends only on the coordinates in $J$: any two inputs agreeing on $J$ have the same value.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on sign vectors of length $n$
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$
